text_blocks.snippet: Federal prosecutors and state officials have issued urgent warnings regarding a wave of fraudulent phone calls, text messages, and imposter scams circulating throughout Central Illinois.
Common Active Scams in Central Illinois

list.snippet: U.S. Attorney Office Imposter Calls: Scammers spoof phone numbers and use real staff names from the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of Illinois to demand immediate payment or sensitive information under threat of arrest.

DMV and State Police Text Scams: Fraudulent texts claiming to be from the Illinois Secretary of State or the Illinois State Police warn recipients of suspended licenses, unpaid tolls, or traffic violations, pushing users to click malicious payment links.

Jail / Bail Imposter Calls: Scammers target family members of incarcerated individuals, claiming money or equipment (like ankle monitors) must be paid immediately via gift cards, exploiting confusion around state policies.
Storm Repair & "Storm Chaser" Cons: Scammers pressure homeowners into paying high upfront costs for unverified post-storm home or roof repairs following seasonal severe weather.
Practice the Pause: Take a step back and independently verify any urgent or threatening communication rather than reacting instantly.
Never Pay via Gift Card: Law enforcement, courts, and government agencies will never demand payment via gift cards, wire transfers, or cryptocurrency.
Do Not Click Links: Delete unsolicited texts regarding traffic fines or toll fees; state agencies do not send unprompted payment text messages.
